title: Diagnostic: Protocol Type Hides Members
hints: Through a protocol type, you can only use the protocol's members.
Call the `Car`-only method directly on the `any Vehicle` parameter.
jsBridge: Through `any Vehicle` you can only call what the protocol declares, the same as a TS variable typed as an interface. To reach `openSunroof()` you downcast (`as? Car`), which is where the design question starts.

compass.q: TS also hides extra members behind an interface type. What's the Swift equivalent of a TS type guard?
Downcasting from `any Vehicle` vs adding the method to the protocol vs generics `<V: Vehicle>`: which respects the abstraction?
With `func commute<V: Vehicle>(_ v: V)`, can you call `openSunroof()`? Why not?
When you find yourself downcasting a protocol a lot, what does that suggest about your abstraction?
